reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any complete real inner product space, equipped with its induced norm, and let f:E→ℝ be everywhere Fréchet differentiable and convex on E. For every pair of nonnegative real numbers β and δ, suppose the actual Riesz gradient of f is β-Lipschitz: ‖∇f(x)−∇f(y)‖≤β‖x−y‖ for all x,y∈E. Then for every u∈E, define W:E→ℝ by W(x)=f(x)+(δ/2)‖x−u‖². The function W is everywhere Fréchet differentiable and δ-strongly convex on E: for all x,y∈E and t∈[0,1], W((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)W(x)+tW(y)−(δ/2)t(1−t)‖x−y‖². For every x∈E its actual Riesz gradient satisfies ∇W(x)=∇f(x)+δ(x−u). Furthermore this gradient is (β+δ)-Lipschitz on E: ‖∇W(x)−∇W(y)‖≤(β+δ)‖x−y‖ for every x,y∈E. Both β and δ may equal zero; the theorem assumes neither finite dimensionality nor existence of any minimizer.
